html:
The Republic of Turkey is the state founded in Anatolia in 1923 from the ruins of the Ottoman Empire. On the 1930 map it is seven years old.

After defeat in the First World War, the Allies planned to carve up Anatolia. A national movement led by Mustafa Kemal fought Greek, Armenian and French forces and won. The Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 fixed the new borders, and the republic was declared that October, with Ankara as capital. Over a million Orthodox Christians and some 400,000 Muslims were moved in the population exchange with Greece.

The 1920s brought fast change from the top:

  • 1922 and 1924: the sultanate and then the caliphate abolished.
  • 1926: a civil code based on Switzerland's.
  • 1928: the Latin alphabet replaces Arabic script.
  • 1934: women get the vote in national elections, and everyone takes a surname.

The later state is on the page Turkey.
